DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 90 s. 2021 JUL 19 DIR. JOSEPHINE CABRIDO-LEYSA Regional Director DILG-Region XII Prime Regional Government Center Carpenter Hill, Koronadal City Dear Dir. Cabrida-Leysa: This has reference to your Letter dated 9 June 2021 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on Resolution No. 2021-05-17-02 passed by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Kidapawan City, entitled "A RESOLUTION SEEKING FOR LEGAL OPINION FROM SECRETARY EDUARDO ANO, DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DILG) THROUGH MS. JULIA JUDITH GEVESO, CITY DIRECTOR, DILG, KIDAPAWAN CITY OFFICE, ON THE AUTHORITY OF HON. JIVY ROE C. BOMBEO, CITY VICE MAYOR OF KIDAPAWAN CITY AND PRESIDING OFFICER OF THE 8TH SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD OF KIDAPAWAN TO ISSUE MEMORANDA CALLING OFF THE CONDUCT OF SPECIAL SESSIONS CALLED FOR BY THE LOCAL CHIEF EXECUTIVE." Per your representation, the whole controversy emanated from the alleged invalid enactment of Appropriation Ordinance of Kidapawan City. Vice Mayor Bombeo posits that there were irregularities in the session conducted when the said ordinance was deliberated, and there are substantial and procedural infirmities in its enactment. However, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Cotabato declared said ordinance operative. The LGU of Kidapawan City is requesting for legal opinion on the acts of Vice Mayor Bombeo, that he pre-emptively denied the Call for Special Session to deliberate a certified urgent matter by the City Mayor. Hence, the herein query.

We would like to inform you that this Department agrees with your position that Vice Mayor Bombeo is without basis to call-off the special session to deliberate a certified urgent matter by the City Mayor, citing as basis thereof this Department's Legal Opinion No. 52, Series of 2019, which cited DILG Opinion No. 27, s. 2009, to wit: "The LGC recognizes the competence of the local chief executive to certify as urgent any ordinance or resolution to be passed by the sanggunian. However, the LGC and its IRR failed to categorically specify as to what ordinances and/or resolutions should be certified as urgent. Neither is there any fixed measure or, at the very least, any instance or controlling condition that will give rise to the certification as urgent of any passage of an ordinance or resolution. The authority vested upon a local chief executive certifying as urgent any legislative matter is granted by law in order to allow LGUs, at the instance of the local chief executive, to respond quickly, through legislative measures, any exigency of public service, public emergency, or calamity which requires immediate attention and solution." Moreover, Section 52(b) of the LGC is explicit that when public interest so demands, special sessions may be called by the local chief executive or by a majority of the members of the sanggunian. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, Y AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: RINGAN Under ecretary for Local Government LS/90
